decoys.why_not_a_defect: The catch guards purely cosmetic path resolution; the fallback (print the path as typed) is correct and the reason is documented. It hides no failure the caller needs; whether the write succeeded is decided elsewhere (the real swallow is T1 in writeExportFile).

candidate.problem: writeExportFile swallows any mkdir/writeFile failure (it only logs, and only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set) and returns normally. runHistoryExport then proceeds as if the write succeeded: line 131 prints 'exported N run(s) to <file>' and exitCode stays 0. Error-handling Rule 3 / Iron Law 1: a catch that hides a failure from a caller who then proceeds is forbidden. This is the only call site.
candidate.impact: A user exporting to an unwritable or invalid path (read-only dir, path under an existing file, full disk) is told the export succeeded and gets exit 0; scripts and flow journals that attach the file find it missing or stale. Fix: let the error propagate (or rethrow with the target path and cause) and set exitCode 1.
